title: Juniper and the Sigil
premise: Juniper Delacroix, daughter of gatekeeper Sebastian, has spent her life keeping ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things—memories, years, names—while her father guards a gate that must never open. When a dying stranger presses a map into Juniper's hands, she learns the covenant binding the two realms is failing because her family's inheritance was built on an unpaid debt: her mother's life, traded to seal the gate. Pursued by guild enforcers and guided by the stranger's ghost, Juniper must reforge the covenant by offering what she inherited—the key written into her own blood. In the end, she pays not with death but with memory, surrendering every recollection of her father and their life together so the gate can close honestly, choosing duty while leaving love as the price that survives her.
about_author: Rosalind Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate papers and unclaimed inheritances, an obsession that bleeds into her fiction. She writes fantasy about bargains, ledgers, and the people who keep them, from a rain-dark coastal town.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She audits the guild's ledger of traded memories and years beneath her father's silent watch, establishing their careful invisibility. A dying stranger collapses at the counting-house door and presses a bloodstained map into her hands before dissolving into salt. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in a carefully maintained ordinary life.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He recognizes the map as his dead wife's handwriting and forbids Juniper from following it, revealing only that the covenant between realms was sealed with a debt he has hidden for twenty years. Juniper defies him, copying the map before he burns it. Emotional beat: betrayal and the ache of paternal protection curdling into control.

chapters.title: Salt and Ash Road
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She flees along the coast road, pursued by guild enforcers led by the elegant Mr. Vane, who wants the map to seize the gate for the guild. The stranger's ghost begins appearing to her, offering fragments of guidance at a cost of her own memories. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Guild of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, with Vane interludes. Captured briefly, Juniper reads the guild's master ledger and discovers her mother's entry: one life, traded to seal the covenant, signed by Sebastian. Vane offers her truth in exchange for the map. Emotional beat: grief weaponized—she takes the bargain without giving up the map.

chapters.title: A Door in the Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following the map to a drowned chapel, she meets Wren, a smuggler who once ferried goods through the gate and lost a brother to it. Their wary alliance kindles into something tender even as the ghost warns that loving anyone is collateral the covenant will claim. Emotional beat: love arriving exactly when it is most dangerous.

chapters.title: The Debt Made Flesh
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crossing the tidal flats, they are ambushed by Vane; the ghost spends most of its remaining substance saving them, revealing it is Juniper's mother, bound to the gate since the trade. Juniper learns the key to reforging the covenant is written in her inherited blood. Emotional beat: devastating recognition—family was the price all along.

chapters.title: Vane's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. He reaches the gate first with guild forces, intending to hold it open and monopolize trade in impossible things, arguing that covenants are just unpriced markets. Sebastian arrives, having abandoned his post for the first time in twenty years, to stand between Vane and his daughter. Emotional beat: cold ideology against stubborn, belated devotion.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the gate, she attempts the covenant rite, but it demands a full payment: everything she inherited, including her memories of her father and of Wren. As Vane breaches the threshold and the far realm begins bleeding through, she chooses to pay. Emotional beat: climax—love and duty finally demanding opposite things.

chapters.title: Everything She Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The covenant seals; Vane is pulled through as collateral, the gate closes clean, and Juniper wakes whole but hollow, unable to recognize the man weeping beside her or the father who carried her home. Her mother's ghost, freed, leaves one final gift: a single preserved memory, hidden where only a ledger-keeper would look. Emotional beat: aftermath—grief and grace entangled.

chapters.title: A New Entry in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue. Months later, Juniper keeps the guild's ledgers honestly now, trading fairly, with Wren patiently courting a woman who doesn't remember falling for him. She finds her mother's hidden memory—a single afternoon of the three of them together—and must choose whether to spend it. She reads it once, then refiles it, choosing to carry forward on faith. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—inheritance reclaimed as choice, not burden.
